HYDRAULIC TUBES OR LINES 0.2 (5.08)
*[1] *[1] Measured at the position where the hose is closest
to the cable or linkage.
6) Support - Make sure the hose assembly is held by supports that will not cause
deflection of rigid lines if movement occurs. Use sufficient clamps to follow the
contour of the structure. This prevents hose abrasive wear, kinks, and entanglement
during flexure. At a minimum, put clamps at locations where the tube clamps were.
Make sure the hose is not rigidly held by tight, rigid clamps about its outer diameter.
If the hose between the rigid connections must move longitudinally, make sure the
clamps are of a type that will not cause wear on the hose casing. The supports must
hold the connections at the tube, not the hose.
20-10-52
SUBTASK 20-10-52-860-002
(5) Remove the pressure from the hydraulic system where you will do the repair. To remove the
pressure, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or
Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-350-001
(6) If you will replace all of the damaged tube with a flexible hose, do these steps:
(a) Remove the damaged tube.
(b) If it is necessary, prepare the ends of the tubes to which you will install the flexible hose.
For selection of the applicable fittings, do this task: Flareless Fittings in Pressurized,
Strut, Fuel T ank, and Cargo Areas Installation, TASK 20-10-51-000-802.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-300-002
(7) If the damaged tube is too long to be replaced by a flexible hose, do these steps:
(a) Cut the damaged tube section from the line.
(b) Install the applicable fittings on the tubes. To install them, do this task: Flareless Fittings
in Pressurized, Strut, Fuel T ank, and Cargo Areas Installation, TASK 20-10-51-000-802.
(c) Install the tubing on the fittings.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-860-003
(8) Supply the usual pressure to the line.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-210-003
(9) Do a check of the hose and the connections for leaks.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-200-002
(10) Do a check to make sure the slack, flex, twisting, bending, clearance, and support is correct.
20-10-52-300-803Temporary Repair of Flexible Hydraulic HosesPDF p. 434

3. Temporary Repair of Flexible Hydraulic Hoses
(Figure 802 and Figure 803)
A. General
(1) This task is for the temporary repair of flexible hydraulic hoses with a different flexible hose.
(a) It is to the discretion of the operator to determine whether this task is applicable to their
operations.
(2) The Boeing Company recommends that the operator do these steps:
(a) Make a record of the flexible hoses that you install as temporary repairs for flexible lines.
(b) Make a schedule for the regular inspection of flexible hose installations.
1) Make sure that the installation stays in an airworthy condition until the system is put
back to its original configuration.
(c) Create a plan to ensure that the flexible hoses that are installed as temporary repairs are
replaced as soon as possible.
1) You must replace the hoses no later than the scheduled removal time determined
by the assigned principal maintenance inspector.
(3) This task is not applicable for replacement of hydraulic hoses on the engines. In general,
hydraulic hoses with damaged firesleeves must be replaced.
(a) Engine hydraulic hoses are hoses below or forward of the firewall and within the engine
cowls.
(4) Hoses in the hydraulic tubing repair kit, SPL-5276, or equivalent, can be used when
temporarily replacing a damaged hydraulic hose with another hydraulic hose.
B. References
Reference Title
29-00-00 P/B 201 HYDRAULIC POWER - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
C. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-5276 Repair Kit, Hydraulic Tubing (3000 psi) (Approved for Titanium)
Part #: 65-92528-11 (Spares Kit) Supplier: 81205
Part #: 65-92528-37 (Spares Kit) Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: 65-92528-1 (Spares Kit) Supplier: 81205
D. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 20-10-52-300-003
(1) Choose a flexible hose to do the temporary repair.
(a) Choose a flexible hose that is qualified for at least the same operating pressure,
temperature, and fluid type as the system in which you will install the flexible hose.
(b) Make sure that the new flexible hose has the same inner diameter (or a larger inner
diameter) as the original flexible hose.
(c) Make sure that the end fitting sizes and configurations (such as straights, 45 degree
bends, or 90 degree bends) on the replacement hose match those of the original flexible
hose (Figure 802).
20-10-52
1) You can do expansion using one of the methods as follows:
a) Use a hose assembly with expander end fittings.
b) Use a non-expander replacement hose assembly and reconnectable fittings
that have different size ends to make the transition.
(d) Make sure that the new flexible hose meets the installation requirements for the items as
follows (Figure 803):
1) Slack
a) Make sure that you do not install the flexible hose in a way that will cause a
mechanical load on the hose.
NOTE: Hoses will change length from +2/-4 percent when pressurized.
2) Flex
a) Make sure that there is slack between the rigid fittings where hose assemblies
will be exposed to vibration or flexing.
b) Make sure that the hose is straight for at least two hose diameters from the
end fittings.
NOTE: This will help make sure that the hose will not flex at the end fittings.
c) Make sure that you do not use clamps at locations that will stop the hose from
flexing.
3) Twisting
a) Make sure that you install the hoses without twists.
NOTE: This will help prevent loose nuts and rupture of the hoses.
<1> Use swivel fittings with positioning ends at one or two ends of the
temporary replacement hose, if it is necessary (Figure 802).
NOTE: This will help to closely match the configuration of the original
hose and will help relieve the twist stresses.
4) Bending
a) Use elbow fittings, hoses with elbow type end fittings or the applicable end
fittings, or the applicable bend radii (Table 803).
NOTE: This will help prevent sharp bends in the hose assembly.
Table 803/20-10-52-993-810

MEASURED AT INNER BEND (INCH)

<1> Make sure to take into account the change in allowable minimum bend

<a> For replacement with hoses that have “C” coded sleeves,
multiply the minimum hose bend radii by 1.2 to calculate the

20-10-52
5) Clearance
a) Make sure that the hose assembly is clear of all other lines, equipment, and
adjacent structure under all operating conditions.
b) Make sure that the hoses meet the minimum clearance requirements in

6) Support

NOTE: This will help prevent contact with the mating or adjacent parts due to

<1> Size clamps as necessary.
NOTE: This will help to account for change in the hose diameter from

E. Flexible Hydraulic Hoses Installation
SUBTASK 20-10-52-040-001
(1) Remove hydraulic pressure from the system on which you will do a repair
(PAGEBLOCK 29-00-00/201).
SUBTASK 20-10-52-020-002
(2) Remove the damaged hose.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-420-007
(3) If you can replace all of the damaged hose with one flexible hose, install the new temporary
flexible hose.
SUBTASK 20-10-52-420-008
(4) If the damaged hose in too long to replace by one flexible hose, do these steps:
(a) Use two or three shorter hoses to make the necessary length hose.
1) Make sure that you do not use more than three shorter hoses to make the
necessary length hose.
(b) Use a union or smaller fitting as a splice between the shorter hoses.
20-10-52
(c) Make sure that the total length of the two or three shorter hoses and splice fittings is
close to the length of the original, damaged hose.
NOTE: A total length that is too long will create kinks or bends in the hoses; a total length
too short will create a tension load on the hoses.
(d) Use the necessary installation torque on the mating hoses and splice fittings.

20-10-72-200-801Coaxial Cable and Antenna System Inspection with a Frequency Domain ReflectometerPDF p. 452
Open original AMM PDF - page 452 ↗ 
3. Coaxial Cable and Antenna System Inspection with a Frequency Domain Reflectometer
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) This procedure has steps to do a health check of a Radio Frequency (RF) system’s coaxial
cables and antenna. This procedure can be done on the entire unit or on individual
components.
(2) You can use a frequency domain reflectometer, COM-15185 to locate opens, shorts, incorrect
crimps, bends, moisture, loose connectors, and defective antenna elements that lead to weak
or intermittent RF operation. You can also use the Frequency Domain Reflectometer (FDR) to
test the antenna elements from the equipment rack for troubleshooting or directly at the
antenna to make sure that reliable operation prior to installation.
(3) The FDR performs a Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) test by transmitting a continuous
RF sweep of the cables and antenna at their operating frequencies and then monitoring the
absorption of the wave by the antenna. The FDR identifies standing or reflected waves due to
loose connections, corrosion, moisture, or defective cable, or faulty antenna which changes
the system impedance resulting in a reflected or standing wave. Standing waves not only
decrease output transmission, resulting in weak, intermittent operation, but may also harm the
transmitter if the reflection is quite large. The recommended FDR is an easy to use handheld
tester, with a Go/No-Go function by use of a limit line and simple distance to fault
measurement. It can be used to quickly identify improper connections, defective cables and
faulty antennas easily from the Equipment rack, eliminating disassembly of the airplane to test
the RF system.
(4) Refer to the Instruction or Operation Manual of the frequency domain reflectometer,
COM-15185, and radio frequency adapter kit, COM-17510 for specific instructions on set-up
and tests for the coaxial cable and antenna system.
NOTE: The Kit P/N 7003A001-4 includes SiteHawk Analyzer P/N SK-6000 TC and Radio
Frequency Adapter Kit P/N 4240-401.
(a) To do a health check of the entire coaxial cable and antenna system, you must remove
the black box from the Electronic Equipment (EE) rack and connect the tester directly to
the rack’s bench plug coax receptacle. There is no need to make any other
disconnections unless the health check fails. The check will give a simple Go/No-Go
indication of the health of the entire cable and antenna system. In the case of a No-Go
indication, any faults may be isolated via the FDR’s “distance to fault” function. Use the
“distance to fault” readout and applicable system wire diagram to help isolate the failure
to a specified connector, cable segment or antenna.
(b) The FDR facilitates both simple Go/No-Go testing, as well as in depth testing. Use the
Instruction or Operation Manual for specific instructions to:
1) DATA SAVE: Stores parameters and able to upload from a Universal Serial Bus
(USB) or via Bluetooth. User can recall settings and immediately test. For example:
User selects “SATCOM High Gain Transmit VSWR” and then plugs into bench
connector and reads display.
2) PROGRAMMING: Provides means to create simple Go/No-Go testing.
3) CALIBRATION: Use the OSL Calibration Compo (Open, Short, 50 ohm Load 50
ohm) to calibrate prior to use.
4) VSWR and RETURN LOSS (RL) TESTING: Displays the readings in Return Loss
(RL) or VSWR, the user simply selects the display they desire.
20-10-72
5) DISTANCE TO FAULT : Displays distance in ft/in or M/cm to the VSWR or RL fault
without disconnecting.

D. System Test with the Antenna Connected
SUBTASK 20-10-72-860-002
(1) Do these steps to prepare the applicable cable, antenna system, and the frequency domain
reflectometer, COM-15185 for testing:
(a) Push the Power button for 5 seconds.
1) Unit will automatically boot into the Sitehawk Analyzer's Measure Match Application.
(b) Press File Cabinet icon (three square dots) to recall previously saved set-up or manually
input settings.
20-10-72
1) SiteHawk status, calibration result, and tracing data can be saved to the instrument,
and can be recalled to be displayed on the sweep display area. The parameters for
this instrument setting include the scale, trace, cursor and analysis. These
parameters are saved in the status files. Data in STATUS+CAL (cst) or STATUS
(sta) data files can be recalled and displayed with the current data trace.
NOTE: STATUS+CAL (cst) files will save the settings and calibration if the unit was
calibrated when the file was saved. STATUS (sta) files only save the setting,
but not calibration.
a) Push the FILE icon to display the file menu. See (Figure 201).
b) Push the Save Type to select file type STATUS+CAL (.cst) or STATUS (.sta).
c) Select Load.
d) Select the data file from the list.
e) Push Load.
NOTE: The active and the recalled trace data will be displayed together in the
sweep display area. In the example, Tr1 is the active trace, the
recalled trace data is indicated with OFF and the file name.
f) Push OFF to remove the recalled trace data.
2) Select MEASURE MATCH MODE.
a) Push trace measurement field to display menu.
b) Select SWR from the Measurement Mode menu.
NOTE: When making a match measurement, select Standing Wave Ratio
(SWR) units for the Y (vertical) scale.
c) Select the number of Data Measurement points (default to 801).
d) Set the Frequency range:
NOTE: Changing the frequency settings will automatically turn the calibration
off. You always set the frequency before calibrating the unit. Once
start/stop frequencies are entered manually, be sure to follow
instructions to calibrate prior to use.
<1> Set start and stop frequencies for the applicable RF system under test
using (Table 201).
<a> Example - For Satellite Communications System (SATCOM)
Transmit (Uplink) Circuit, set the start/stop frequency at a wider
span the system’s frequency range as specified in the chart. The
chart shows that the start/stop frequency should be set at a
minimum of 1600 MHz and 1700 MHz to test the system’s
operating frequency of 1626.5 MHz and 1660.5 MHz.
20-10-72
3) CALIBRATE: For best results, you can set the frequency and calibrate the Bird Site
Analyzer immediately before taking measurements.
NOTE: Use a precision open, short, load (OSL) calibration standard or “Calibration
Combo" for accurate measurement results.
NOTE: When using an extension cable, a phase stable cable is needed to ensure
performance and accuracy. Connect the RF test cable and the adapter
(extension) and then calibrate to the end of this extension. If the cable or
adapters are removed, you must calibrate again.
NOTE: Changing frequency settings will automatically turn calibration off. Always
set the frequency before calibrating the unit.
a) Push the Calibrate icon.
b) Connect the Cal Combo “Open” connector to the end of the extension cable’s
bench connector adapter.
c) Push the Open softkey.
d) Wait for the unit to sweep and a Green Check to display.
e) Connect the Cal Combo “Short” connector to the end of the extension cable’s
bench connector adapter.
f) Wait for the unit to sweep and a Green Check to display.
g) Connect the Cal Combo “Load” connector to the end of the extension cable’s
bench connector adapter.
h) Push the Load softkey.
i) Wait for the unit to sweep and a Green Check to display.
NOTE: During calibration, the color of the icon display is yellow.
NOTE: Whenever the SiteHawk has been calibrated, a COR ON indicator is
shown in the lower right corner of the display. Anytime the frequency is
changed, the calibration is turned OFF and the COR ON disappears,
requiring the unit to be recalibrated.
4) The limit line helps to set off those parts of a trace that are outside of the
acceptance (limit) values. It shows as a red horizontal line at the limit line value. The
part of the trace that is not acceptable will display in white. The signals which fall
outside the acceptable limits can be identified with a failure flag and an alarm. Use
(Table 201) to set the limit to the Max VSWR for the RF system under test.
a) Push the Limit Icon.
b) Select Limit (On/Off). Push to toggle the limit line On and Off.
c) Set Value. Sets the position of the limit line on the vertical scale (Y axis). Push
the field to enter a value.

20-10-75-700-801Thermal Imaging ChecksPDF p. 467
Open original AMM PDF - page 467 ↗ 
2. Thermal Imaging Checks
A. General
(1) Recommended Equipment
(a) An infrared camera, COM-15040 is the recommended equipment. When performing
electrical system tests, it is recommended to use an infrared camera, COM-15040 with a
high temperature range and low thermal sensitivity (also known as Noise Equivalent
T emperature Difference (NETD)) of ≤ 32°F at 86°F (≤ 0.05°C at 30°C). It is also
recommended to use an infrared camera, COM-15040 with auto focus and auto ranging
to enable ease of use and consistent testing.
(2) Usage
(a) Thermal imaging is a qualitative inspection that focuses on temperature differences as
opposed to actual temperatures. Look for differences between equivalent components in
equivalent load conditions. This can be compared to a recorded database or another
operational system, such as duplicate system (left or right), or another aircraft.
1) It is good to keep your measurements while you record the load conditions at the
time of each scan. This will allow you to create a database and properly evaluate
your measurements against normal operating conditions.
(3) Images in this task are examples only. The images may not agree with your airplane model or
airplane configuration.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
COM-15040 Camera - Infrared
Part #: FLK-TI480-PRO Supplier: 4U744
Opt Part #: T440 Supplier: 093V7
Opt Part #: TI400 Supplier: 89536
Opt Part #: TI450 Supplier: 89536
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 20-10-75-750-001
(1) Electrical Tests
(a) Thermal imaging (TI) may be used to identify the location of electrical system faults using
an infrared camera, COM-15040 to identify three basic thermal patterns associated with
electrical failure:
1) High resistance caused by poor surface contact such as loose, corroded,
over-tightened, over/under crimped, dirty contacts. These conditions decrease
electron flow and cause the connection to become hot.
20-10-75
2) A short, over-loaded circuit or multi-phase imbalance problem. Shorts or
unbalanced loads cause increased electron flow, increasing heat flow in the wiring
to the load.
3) An open circuit is viewed as a cool connection. An open contact, switch, or blown
fuse may be easily identified by a cool indication (Figure 201 (Sheet 1)).
(b) Inspect connections and wiring.
1) Operate the system with the highest possible load (min 40%), and try to point the
infrared camera, COM-15040 as perpendicular to the object as possible for
consistent readings.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR PERSONAL PROTECTIVE
EQUIPMENT WHEN OPENING PANELS AND INSPECTING HIGH
POWER SOURCES. IF YOU DO NOT WEAR THE PERSONAL
PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT , INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
2) Use the infrared camera, COM-15040 to easily examine wiring and connections.
Opening of panels or enclosures can be necessary for a direct view of the
connections.
3) Look for connections that have a higher temperature indication compared with
equivalent connections under equivalent loads. This could indicate a loose, over
tightened, over/under crimped terminals, broken wiring strands, or corroded
connections with increased resistance.
a) Connection-related hot spots usually appear warmest at the spot of highest
resistance, cooling with distance from that spot. Notice whether the heat
continues back along the wire toward the connection (connection-related
problem) or toward the load (load related problem).
b) In some cases a cold component is abnormal because of the current being
shunted away from the high-resistance connection. You can also find broken
or undersized wires or defective insulation.
4) Per the NETA (International Electrical Testing Association) guidelines, a difference in
temperature (DT) between similar components under similar loads exceeding 25°F
or 14°C, requires further investigation.
a) Upon identifying a hot spot, isolation of the root cause may be done with
standard tooling (multi-meter, ammeter) to verify if caused by a loose
connection, dirty relay contact, etc. (Figure 202 (Sheet 1)).
(c) Examine Fuses
1) If a fuse shows up hot on a thermal scan, it may be at or near its current capacity.
But, not all problems are hot. A blown fuse, or an open circuit for example, would
produce a cooler than normal temperature (Figure 203 (Sheet 1)).
(d) Inspect Motor Control Center (MCC) or Common Motor Start Controller (CMSC)
1) To evaluate a MCC or CMSC under load, open up each compartment and compare
the relative temperatures of key components: bus bars, controllers, starters,
contactors, relays, fuses, breakers, disconnects, feeders, and transformers.
Incorporate the guidelines above for examination of connections and fuses and
identification of phase imbalance (Figure 204 (Sheet 1)).
(e) Examine Three-Phase Circuits
20-10-75
1) Compare all three phases, side- by-side, and check for temperature differences
exceeding 25°F or 14°C. A cooler than-normal circuit or leg might signal a failed
component. More heavily loaded phases will show warmer. Hot conductors may be
undersized, overloaded, or have a defective connections as described above.
Voltage drops across fuses, circuit breakers, and relay contacts can also create an
unbalanced condition, prematurely damaging the motor. Follow the unwanted heat
to the root trouble spot. Before you assume that the cause has been found, verify
with a multi-meter or clamp-on ammeter (Figure 205 (Sheet 1)).
(f) Examine Pitot Static Probe/AOA Sensor Heating Elements
1) Check for partially open or shorted heating elements which are known to cause
intermittent operation in flight.
a) T echnician A, prepare a infrared camera, COM-15040 by focusing on target
before you turn on probe heat.
b) T echnician B, turn on probe heat
c) T echnician A, use infrared camera, COM-15040 to watch probes come up to
temperature.
<1> Good Pitot Static probe will display the hottest point at the tip with probe
element visible, then gradually cooling moving towards the base.
<2> Good AOA Sensor will display an outboard half nearly the same temp,
then gradually cooling toward the base (Figure 206 (Sheet 1)).
(g) Pressurization Leak Tests
1) An infrared camera, COM-15040, with the recommended sensitivity above, easily
picks up temperature differences > 0.5°F or 0.3°C between air inside and outside
the airplane. This allows identification of leaking windows, door seals, and outflow
valves.
a) When the aircraft is pressurized, technician A should walk around the aircraft
identifying possible leaks with the infrared camera, COM-15040. Make sure to
monitor the actual temperatures displayed on the infrared camera,
COM-15040.
b) T echnician B, in communication with technician A, verifies leaks using an
ultra-sonic leak detector and marks the location (Figure 207 (Sheet 1)).
(h) Pack Leak Tests
1) Troubleshoot pack operation by identifying proper flow and leaks.
a) Operate both packs
b) View Air Cycle Machine (ACM) compressor and turbine operation and
compare with the other side.
c) View the heat exchanger and compare it with the one on the other side.
d) Look for the correct operation of the ACM & heat exchanger and leaks.
2) See example below of too hot air exiting turbine 65°F (18°C) turbine outlet and
130°F (54°C) plenum inlet than left side. Found right pack HEX leaking (Figure 208
(Sheet 1)).
(i) Bleed Air Leak Tests
1) Chronic and intermittent bleed air leaks can be found with thermal imaging.
20-10-75
a) Before you apply bleed air, walk around aircraft with the infrared camera,
COM-15040. Record anomalies in potential leak areas; engine pylon, leading
edges, wing root to pack(s). This is to mitigate confusion because of sun, heat
transfer, and reflective surfaces.
b) Operate the bleed air and walk around the aircraft to identify possible leaks
with the infrared camera, COM-15040. Make sure that you carefully monitor
the actual temperatures that display on the infrared camera, COM-15040.
c) Once you identify a hot area, turn off bleed air and remove panels to further
isolate them with the infrared camera, COM-15040.
d) Once panel is removed, bleed air leaks are easily pinpointed to clamps, valve
body, seals, etc. (Figure 209 (Sheet 1)).
(j) Hydraulic Tests
1) Thermography permits visualization of hydraulic fluid flow; readily identifying proper
heat exchanger operation, leaks, valve condition (open, closed, partially
open/closed), oil filter bypass condition, accumulator pre-charge level, reservoir
contamination, and hydraulic bypassing within a component.
a) Examine the heat exchanger operation by viewing flow of hot to cold fluid.
Record temperature and compare with other side, or previously recorded
database.
b) Inspect for a filter bypass condition by viewing filter for marked temperature
drop, indicating bypassing fluid (Figure 210 (Sheet 1)).
c) Inspect for actuator bypass condition by viewing internal leakage (Figure 210
(Sheet 1)).
d) Examine for an incorrect accumulator pre-charge condition
e) Inspect the reservoir for possible contamination (water shows as foam)
(Figure 210 (Sheet 1)).
(k) Water/Mold Detection
1) Sources of moisture, “Rain in the Plane,” and moisture trapped in insulation
blankets may be identified using the infrared camera, COM-15040. Scheduled
inspections to find moisture can prevent catastrophic damage that could be caused
from undetected mold or pools of water (Figure 211 (Sheet 1)).
(l) Fluid Level
1) Fluid levels can be checked without the removal of components. For example, fire
bottles, accumulators, reservoirs, etc. may be easily checked for fluid level and
contamination (Figure 212 (Sheet 1)).
(m) Motor/Pump/Bearings
1) The infrared camera, COM-15040 can be used to identify worn bearings, abnormal
pump flow, bearing lubrication failure, and pump to motor coupling misalignment
that can cause premature wear to bearings (Figure 213 (Sheet 1)).

20-10-76-700-801LE Slat Retract Magnetic Target Check IPDF p. 485
Open original AMM PDF - page 485 ↗ 
2. LE Slat Retract Magnetic Target Check I
A. General
(1) The LE Slats utilize six each two-wire cylindrical proximity sensors (P/N 8-788-02) and
magnetic target for sensors S1094 through S1099. The sensor's impedance rapidly changes
as the magnetic target approaches and retracts. This check ensures a minimum gauss level
from the center of the target in order to eliminate intermittent transient lights due to low target
magnetism when the slats are retracted.
B. References
Reference Title
27-81-00-040-801 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation (P/B 201)
27-81-00-440-801 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats - Activation (P/B 201)
27-81-00-860-803 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Extension (P/B 201)
27-81-00-860-804 Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction (P/B 201)
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-6151 Gaussmeter
STD-12053 Magnetometer (Capable of measuring 65-75 gauss)
D. Location Zones

E. Procedure
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS AND THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS. THE
FLAPS AND SLATS WILL EXTEND. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE INBOARD AND
OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED OR REMOVED BEFORE
YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS IN THIS TEST .
THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO
EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-001
(1) Make sure the inboard fan duct cowl and the inboard and outboard thrust reversers are closed
or removed before extending the leading edge flaps and slats.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-002

Edge Flaps and Slats Extension, TASK 27-81-00-860-803.

MAKE SURE THAT YOU DEACTIVATE THE LEADING-EDGE SLAT BEFORE
YOU WORK ON THE SLAT SYSTEM. THE SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY
WHEN YOU ACTIVATE THEM. IT CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT .
(3) To deactivate the leading edge flaps and slats in the full extend position, do this task: Leading
Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801,
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-002
(4) Use gaussmeter, STD-6151 or magnetometer, STD-12053 to test each slat retract sensor
magnetic target, S1094 through S1099, and complete Table 201.
(a) Obtain readings with gaussmeter, STD-6151 or magnetometer, STD-12053 by:
1) Selecting “Max” to retain the maximum value, the display will keep updating as
higher value is recorded while moving the meter to and from the target; at least 3
times.
2) Position the meter to measure the electromagnetic waves. Try to change the
measurement angle or position to obtain the highest reading value. (Figure 201).
3) Make sure that a minimum of 600mG per target.

(8) Set up the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741 as follows:
(a) Push the L/C/R mode switch to set to R (resistance mode).
(b) Push the 1 kHz/120Hz button to select the 120Hz excitation frequency.
(c) Push the DATA HOLD button once.
(d) Push and hold the L/C/R button until the meter changes to the series mode.
NOTE: “Ser” appears in the upper right corner of the display to indicate that the meter is
in the series mode.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-009
(9) Read and record the resistance value on the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance,
Resistance), COM-1741.
NOTE: The Nominal Resistance reading at normal room temperature (CMM DC resistance,
bench test condition) referred to as L1. L1 should be 27 to 33 ohms (+2 ohms for
wiring = 29 to 35 ohms). The permitted resistance reading for in-service sensors
exposed to varying conditions is 24 to 38 ohms. The Nominal Resistance reading at
normal room temperature (CMM DC resistance, bench test condition) referred to as
R1. R1 should be 344.5 to 351.5 ohms (+2 ohms for wiring = 346.5 to 353.5 ohms).
The permitted resistance reading for in-service sensors exposed to varying conditions
is 338 to 361 ohms. The Nominal Resistance reading at normal room temperature
(CMM DC resistance, bench test condition) referred to as C1. C1 should be
approximately 32 ohms. The permitted resistance reading for in-service sensors
exposed to varying conditions is 20 to 100 ohms.
On wing resistance readings will vary with the temperature of the proximity sensor. The
resistance values can be outside the permitted limits and the proximity sensor can still
be serviceable. The copper metal has a temperature coefficient of resistance that is
approximately 0.40 ohm/°C. The deviation of the coil circuit (generally the yellow-red
circuit can be calculated at the rate of 0.40 ohm/°C from the Standard T emperature
(77°F (25°C)).
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-010

(1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 11 C01443 FC TE FLAP POS/SKEW SNSR & IND RIGHT
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-019
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU OPEN THE P6-2 CIRCUIT BREAKER PANEL. THE
P6-2 CIRCUIT BREAKER PANEL CONTAINS HIGH VOLTAGES AND
CURRENTS THAT CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(2) Open P6-2 Right circuit breaker panel.
20-10-76
SUBTASK 20-10-76-480-006
(3) Locate the circuit breaker C01443 on P6-2 panel.
(a) Connect oscilloscope, COM-18639 to either of the circuit breaker's terminals and aircraft
ground.
(b) Connect clamp-on probe, COM-9509 around wire W0044-0562-24.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-020
(4) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 11 C01443 FC TE FLAP POS/SKEW SNSR & IND RIGHT
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-012
(5) Prepare to measure voltage and amperage while moving the TE Flaps from UP to 40 and back
to UP .
(a) Begin recording voltage and amperage to capture spikes, or dropouts or deviation >20%
while flaps are in transit through full range of movement.
(b) Monitor flap position indicator for evidence of lagging, sticking, or leap frogging behavior
in either of the flap position indicator needles.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-021
(6) Extend the flaps from 0 to 40 degrees using hydraulic power. Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap
System Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Record the highest and lowest voltage and current values through the flaps down cycle.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-022
(7) Retract the flaps from 40 to 0 degrees using hydraulic power. Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap
System Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Record the highest and lowest voltage and current values through the flaps up cycle.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-013
(8) Evaluate the following:
(a) Make sure the recorded voltage and current values through the flaps down/up cycle are
within the following readings:
1) Nominal voltage throughout cycle.
a) Voltage = 75VPP to 85VPP or 26VAC to 30VAC.
2) Nominal Amperage throughout cycle.
a) Amperage = 1.0A to 2.0A.
(b) Make sure voltage and current is within nominal range and does not spike or dropout.
Also, ensure voltage and amperage does not deviate (gradually increase or decrease)
from stationary value >20% during transition.
1) Deviation example:
a) Stationary Value = 1.5A
b) In transit deviation must be <20% = 1.5 X 0.2 = deviation range 1.2A to 1.8A
(c) If values exceeds above, or needles were lagging, sticking or leap frogging, recommend
isolating root cause at next maintenance opportunity by performing Trailing Edge (TE)
flap indication fault isolation procedure for faults 27-52259 and 27-52260.
20-10-76

A. General
(1) This task contains the procedure for performing Flap Position Indicator, Flap Position
Transmitters, Flap Skew Sensors and interface wiring Insulation Resistance Predictive health
Check.

Skew Sensor system by comparing the Insulation Resistance (IR) and Dielectric Absorption
Rate (DAR).

WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT USE A POSSIBLE IGNITION SOURCE

STABLE AND CAUSE POSSIBLE IGNITION. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY
TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.

SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-018

(a) During the test, the high voltage symbol will display in the upper left corner and the TEST
icon will show in the lower portion of the meter's screen until the test is finished.
(b) The primary display will show the measured Insulation Resistance (IR) and upon test
completion, the Dielectric Absorption Ratio (DAR).
1) During testing, observe and record the lowest IR value displayed in Table 207.
2) Upon test completion, record the DAR value at the end of the test ( EX. 0.9,
1.0,..1.6, ERR).
NOTE: ERR ≥ 1.6

A. General

(2) The test will determine the condition of the electrical sub-components of the Flap Position and

G. Test Evaluation
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-028
(1) Evaluate each of the test results of resistance tests recorded in Table 208, Table 209 and
Table 210.
20-10-76
(a) For Table 210: If the measured value is outside the resistance requirement range for any
test point and there is no active fault, it is acceptable to not perform any additional
maintenance or component replacement. The airplane can be dispatched without further
maintenance.
(b) If one of the tests does not meet the resistance requirements, it is recommended to do a
fault isolation.
1) Disconnect the applicable LRU.
2) Do the resistance test to isolate between LRU and wiring.
(c) If all of the tests meet the resistance requirements, no more action is necessary.

9. TE Flap Indication Dynamic Health Check With C27110-1
(Figure 202)
A. General
(1) This task contains the procedure for performing Flap Position Indicator, Flap Position
Transmitters, and Flap Skew Sensors dynamic health test utilizing a data acquisition unit and
software.
(2) The health test will determine the condition of the electrical sub-components of the Flap
Position and Skew Sensor system by recording and comparing the supply and output voltages
of the electrical sub-components.
(3) This is an optional procedure and the results are for evaluation purposes only. No action is
required as a result of this inspection. Recommendations made reflect Boeing’s best practices
to ensure maximum aircraft reliability and are optional, so long as a flight deck effect or other
noted system defect does not exist. If a flight deck effect or other noted system defect exists, it
must be corrected in accordance with established processes.
(4) This test requires the removal of the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) to facilitate the test box
interface cable. The Asymmetry Detection, Skew Detection, and Uncommanded Motion (UCM)
Detection that the FSEU offers will be provided by the test box; however, it is critical that the
instructions are followed in this task to prevent damage to the aircraft.

E. TE Flap Indication Dynamic Health Check
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-035
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Primary Control,
TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Operate the flaps through a full cycle, full extend and full retract.
(b) Make sure that the flap system operates smoothly and no flap lock out occurs.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS IF A FLAP
LOCKOUT OCCURS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
(c) If a flap lockout occurs, do these steps:
1) Visually inspect the Trailing Edge (TE) flap for mechanical binding
(TASK 27-51-00-210-801).
2) Make sure that the flap transmission torque brake trip indicators are not extended
(Figure 202).
3) Check the FSEU for existing faults (TASK 27-51-00-740-801).
NOTE: If you are using this task to aid in troubleshooting of a TE flap position
indication system or TE flap skew system, and there are existing faults
displayed in the FSEU, continue with this task.
4) Operate the TE flaps with alternate control (TASK 27-51-00-860-802).
a) If the flaps operate with alternate control, the lockout is considered an
indication lockout.
<1> Continue the test with primary control to operate the flaps.
b) If the flaps do not operate with alternate control, refer to Fault Isolation Manual
(FIM) and do the applicable procedure(s).
20-10-76
SUBTASK 20-10-76-010-006

(a) Install the breakout box assy, C27110-2, SPL-25596, in place of the FSEU.

box assy, C27110-2, SPL-25596.
2) Connect the P1 connector of the cable assy, C27110-3, SPL-25597, to the J1
connector of the test kit, SPL-25095.
(b) Connect the cable assy, C27110-4, SPL-25598.

D686P/J connector.
3) Connect the P2 connector of the cable assy, C27110-4, SPL-25598, to the J2

20-10-76-700-809TE Flap Vibration TestPDF p. 525

11. TE Flap Vibration Test
(Figure 203)
A. General
(1) This task utilizes the wireless vibration test set, SPL-24270, to perform single axis vibration
sensor measurements to determine mechanical health of the component being tested. The
vibration will be measured on each Trailing Edge (TE) Flap Driver Transmission individually. A
high vibration reading indicates lack of lubrication and/or mechanical degradation of the
component(s).
(2) This is an optional procedure, and the results are for evaluation purposes only. No action is
required as a result of this inspection. Recommendations made reflect Boeing’s best practices
to ensure maximum aircraft reliability and are optional, so long as a flight deck effect or other
noted system defect does not exist. If a flight deck effect or other noted system defect exists, it
must be corrected in accordance with established processes.
B. References
Reference Title
12-22-51 P/B 301 TRAILING EDGE FLAP SYSTEM - SERVICING
27-51-00-860-801 Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Primary Control
(P/B 201)
27-51-00-860-804 Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201)
20-10-76

that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.

E. Vibration Data Collection
SUBTASK 20-10-76-470-002
(1) Set up the wireless vibration test set, SPL-24270, to measure vibrations of the TE Flaps.
(a) Open the Boeing Toolbox ReliablePlane application on your iPad.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-860-037
(2) Extend the TE Flaps to 40 degrees (TASK 27-51-00-860-801).
SUBTASK 20-10-76-480-023
(3) Get access to the TE Flap Drive Transmission.
(a) Attach the vibration sensor to the TE Flap Drive.
1) Turn on the sensor by depressing the button on the top of the sensor(s).
2) Configure the Boeing Toolbox ReliablePlane application (Figure 203).
a) Press the SELECT AIRCRAFT and TEST button.
b) Select your Aircraft Model.
c) Enter your Aircraft Identifier.
d) Select ATA Chapter 27.
e) Select ATA Sub System Chapter 51.
f) Select the number of sensors you are using, 1 OR 4.
g) Select the position you are testing.
NOTE: When four sensors are used, selecting position 1, 2, 3, or 4 will test
the left wing and selecting position 5, 6, 7, or 8 will test the right wing.
Only one position needs to be selected.
h) Select the "Next”.
(b) Select the sensor(s) for measurements (Figure 203):
1) For single sensor measurements, do this step:
a) Select the sensor from the pop-up window.
NOTE: The sensor will be listed by WA101 and the last four digits of the serial
number.
2) For four sensor measurements, do these steps:
20-10-76
a) Select an available sensor for each position.
NOTE: All available sensors will be listed in the pop-up window.
NOTE: Each position will be assigned a sensor by WA101 and the last four
digits of the serial number.
NOTE: Once all sensors are assigned, the pop-up window will close, and the
wing diagram will open.
b) Make sure that the position location and last four digits of the serial number on
the sensor match.
(c) Select the “Sensor Location” tab at the top of the screen.
(d) Attach the sensor(s).
NOTE: For the locations shown on photo, the incorrect readings and poor data collection
can occur if the sensor is incorrectly attached or mounting magnet is not
tightened properly.
1) If the illustrated attach point is non ferrous, attach the sensor directly to the ballnut
in a similar manner as positions 4 and 5.
2) If one sensor is used, attach the sensor to the transmission location under test.
3) If four sensors are used, attach them to all transmission locations on wing for the
data collection.
a) Push the ”Position” to verify the location of the sensors.
(e) Select the “Vibration” tab at the top of the screen.
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-037
(4) Collect the vibration data.
NOTE: Data collection must start immediately after TE Flap movement starts, not before it
starts.
(a) Make note of any pop-up messages after the test is complete.
NOTE: It is important to note the position, condition, and component the message is
correlated with.
(b) Retract the TE Flaps to 30 degrees (TASK 27-51-00-860-801).
(c) Select the ”Start Test” as soon as the TE Flaps start to move.
(d) If you are collecting vibration data on multiple TE Flap drive transmissions, return the TE
Flaps to 40 degrees.
(e) Select the “Back” at the top left of the screen.
(f) If it is necessary, select the next component to test.
(g) If it is necessary, repeat steps (3) and (4).
F . Evaluate the Test Results
SUBTASK 20-10-76-700-038
(1) Check the “Overall G” and “Peak G” values on the measurement screen and determine the
alert level using Table 213 (Figure 203 (Sheet 5)).
Table 213/20-10-76-993-816 Recommended Overall G Value Limits
Position Yellow Alert Value Red Alert Value
1 and 8 0.7 to 1.25 G OVERALL and/or 2 to 4 G PEAK > 1.25 G OVERALL and/or > 4 G PEAK
20-10-76
Table 213/20-10-76-993-816 Recommended Overall G Value Limits (Continued)
Position Yellow Alert Value Red Alert Value
2 and 7 0.7 to 1.25 G OVERALL and/or 2 to 4 G PEAK > 1.25 G OVERALL and/or > 4 G PEAK
3 and 6 0.7 to 1.25 G OVERALL and/or 2 to 4 G PEAK > 1.25 G OVERALL and/or > 4 G PEAK
4 and 5 0.7 to 1.25 G OVERALL and/or 2 to 4 G PEAK > 1.25 G OVERALL and/or > 4 G PEAK
(a) If the message “Excessive Bearing Noise Detected” appears during any of your data
collection events, it is recommended that replacement of that transmission, jackscrew,
and ball nut be accomplished at the next convenient maintenance opportunity.
(b) If the value is below 0.7 G Overall and/or 2 G Peak, the system is mechanically sound,
and no further action is recommended.
(c) If the value is between 0.7 to 1.25 G Overall and/or 2 to 4 G Peak, a lack of lubrication is
present, do these steps:
NOTE: When the test is complete, the software will provide a message block to indicate
which component needs lubrication.
1) Lubricate the identified component (PAGEBLOCK 12-22-51/301).
2) Repeat Vibration Data Collection for the flap transmission, jackscrew, and ballnut
that had the Yellow Alert Value.
(d) If the measured vibration amplitude(s) exceed 1.25 G Overall and/or 4 G Peak, do these
steps:
NOTE: When the test is complete, the software will provide a message block to indicate
which component needs lubrication.
1) Lubricate the identified component (PAGEBLOCK 12-22-51/301).
2) Repeat Vibration Data Collection for the flap transmission, jackscrew, and ballnut
that had the Red Alert Value.
3) Replace the applicable ballscrew if vibrations exceed 0.7 units or a flight deck effect
is experienced at your next convenient maintenance opportunity.

3. Pitot Probe Heater Power Consumption Check - Check II
A. General
(1) This task does a check of the power consumption of the pitot probe heater system.
(2) The test will determine the current condition of the electrical sub-components of the pitot probe
system by comparing the power consumption values with the Component Maintenance Manual
(CMM) reference value.
(3) It is recommended to perform this test when there are minimal wind conditions and the ambient
air temperature is between 68°F (20°C) and 86°F (30°C).
(4) The AC amperage value is recorded with an amperage clamp every 60 seconds for a
maximum of 5 minutes.
NOTE: An additional multimeter without the amperage clamp connected can be used to
measure and record the voltage.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers

20-10-77-200-803Pitot Probe Heater Insulation Resistance Check - Check IIIPDF p. 543

4. Pitot Probe Heater Insulation Resistance Check - Check III
A. General
(1) This task includes the steps to perform an Insulation Resistance (IR) Predictive Health Check
on the Pitot Probe, P5-9 Panel and the interface wiring.
(2) Insulation tests should only be performed on de-energized circuits.
(3) The Pitot Probe IR Check requires access to the rear of the probe to disconnect the negative
wires, either by removing the probe or by removing flight deck access panels. Recommend
performing this check concurrently with scheduled maintenance tasks that require the flight
deck access panels to be removed.
(4) The test will determine the condition of the electrical sub-components of the Pitot system by
measuring the IR Dielectric Absorption Rate (DAR).
20-10-77
(a) The DAR test is particularly valuable for uncovering moisture, oil, contaminant ingress
that have a flattening effect on the DAR curve, causing leakage current and eventually
shorted windings. The DAR is the ratio of two time-resistance readings: one is taken after
60 seconds and the other is taken after 30 seconds. With good insulation, the IR will start
low and then increase as the capacitive leakage current and absorption current get
smaller. Results are obtained by dividing the 60 sec test value by the 30 sec test value. A
low DAR index usually indicates problems with the insulation. The recommended
insulation resistance multimeter, COM-17798 or an equivalent, provides an automated
timed test providing a ratio of 60s/30s, to identify moisture or contamination in
connectors, heater windings, and aircraft wiring installations.
(b) Follow instructions to properly evaluate using Table 203 or Table 204.
(5) Review INSULATION RESISTANCE TESTING - INSPECTION/CHECK,
PAGEBLOCK 20-10-39/501, prior to performing this procedure.
(6) Obey all WARNINGS and Cautions during the task.
(7) An insulation resistance multimeter, COM-17798 or an equivalent tool is required for this task.

20-10-78-760-801Power Quality ChecksPDF p. 551
Open original AMM PDF - page 551 ↗ 
2. Power Quality Checks
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) Equipment Recommendation
(a) Fluke 437-II 400 Hz power quality analyzer, COM-15045 or equivalent.
(2) Usage
(a) Enables user to identify the presence of intermittent, transient and unbalanced power
conditions in aircraft systems; i.e. Power sources (Auxiliary Power Unit (APU),Ground
Power Unit (GPU) and ENG GEN (Engine Generator)) and unbalanced loading from
branch circuits. Undiagnosed, this imbalance contributes to nuisance tripping of
ground/universal fault interrupters, circuit breakers. Unbalanced power also results in
high stator winding current leading to overheating and reduced life of 3-Phase
components.
1) The top causes of these conditions are due to loose connections, degraded relay
contacts, unbalanced loads, and overloading.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
COM-15045 Analyzer - Power Quality
Part #: HDPQ XPLORER 400 Plus Supplier: 23207
Part #: PQ3198 Supplier: 1ZJQ1
Opt Part #: FLUKE-437-II Supplier: 89536
Opt Part #: PW3198-01/500 PRO Supplier: 1ZJQ1
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 20-10-78-860-001
(1) Inspect Power Quality
(a) Start by de-energizing the circuit, if possible. Follow local instructions for Lockout/Tagout
(LOTO) and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
(b) Connect analyzer on the supply side first (GPU, APU, ENG GEN), before distribution to
loads.
1) While the analyzer does not disturb any connections, removal of panel(s) will be
necessary to expose individual phase conductors and terminals. The current
clamps [1] and voltage clips [2] must be installed around and on each individual
phase.
a) The current clamps [1] should be placed around all three phases and neutral.
Be sure to connect phase “A” clamp around circuit phase “A”, then “B” around
“B”, etc. Arrow on clamp must point toward the load for proper display.
20-10-78
b) The voltage clips [2] should be attached to an exposed connection (i.e.
terminal block).
c) Connect all 3 phases, neutral and ground.
<1> If circuit is energized, connect ground lead first for safety.
2) Follow analyzer instructions for proper analyzer setting.
(c) Operate only one power generation source (GPU, APU or ENG GEN) at a time.
(d) Place system under load. Follow the corresponding AMM procedure to operate various
high load devices.
1) Operate 3-phase loads; hydraulic pumps, fuel pumps, lighting, etc.
(e) Test for proper connection
1) Select “Volt/Amps/Hertz” screen to make sure readings are within specifications.
a) For example: GPU, APU and ENG GEN voltage and frequency should be
close to the nominal values of 115 V and 400Hz. The APU is 235VAC/400Hz
see SSM/WDM for 115VAC/400Hz connections.
2) Select Scope Button to view waveforms.
a) Make sure the correct waveform for each phase, voltage and frequency.
b) Note any obvious distortion.
3) Select “Phasor” function to ensure correct current clamp hookup to match phase
rotation and note correct phase shift.
a) Voltage is the heavy arrow and current is the thin arrow. Phase current and
volts should be nearly in phase if 180 out of phase, make sure current
clamps [1] arrows are facing toward the load.
b) In a 3-phase power system, the phase shift between voltages and between
currents should be close to 120°.
SUBTASK 20-10-78-700-001
(2) Evaluate Power Quality
(a) Monitor Stable Power.
1) Go back to Volts/Amps/Hertz screen.
a) Check voltage readings for imbalance issues.
<1> Voltage on any one phase should not vary more than 2% of the average
of the 3 phases.
b) Check current readings for imbalance issues.
<1> Current unbalance must not be more than 10 %. In case of too high
unbalance, use other measuring modes, such as “unbalance” mode, to
further analyze the power system.
2) Go to scope, Phasor and trend screens to evaluate distortion, unbalance phase,
and intermittent spikes.
(b) Monitor Power Transition - Continue monitoring as above.
1) While maintaining the same load, switch between individual power sources; GPU,
APU and ENG GEN.
2) Look for smooth transitions and comparable readings.
SUBTASK 20-10-78-810-001
(3) Fault Analysis
20-10-78
(a) If a fault exists when using only one of the generating systems (GPU, APU or ENG GEN):
1) Fault may exist
a) Internal to the generating source.
b) Between the generating source, and the aircraft bus tie contactor terminal
connection.
2) See troubleshooting section to isolate faulty component.
(b) If a fault exists when using multiple sources; GPU and APU, or GPU and ENG GEN, or
APU and ENG GEN:
1) Isolate problem between applicable aircraft bus tie contactors, and loads:
a) Cycle individual loads one at a time, hydraulic pumps, fuel pumps, etc. Until
the unbalanced load circuit is identified.
2) See troubleshooting section to isolate faulty components.
SUBTASK 20-10-78-700-002
(4) Troubleshooting
(a) Circuit analysis
1) Follow local instructions for LOTO and PPE throughout this section.
2) De-energize the circuit, if possible, and move the analyzer if necessary to continue
the fault isolation procedure.
3) Use the analyzer’s “Unbalance”, “In Rush”, and “Trend” modes to isolate fault to an
individual circuit.
a) “Unbalance” mode offers a Meter, Scope, Trend, and a Phasor display.
b) “In Rush” mode allows inspection of 3-phase components high current draw
due to a degrading pump/motor or internal connection.
c) “Trend” mode allows identification of transient faults.
SUBTASK 20-10-78-700-003
(5) Component Analysis
(a) Once an individual source circuit (GPU, APU, ENG GEN) or load circuit (i.e. “Boost Pump
CTR T ank Left”) is identified as the cause of the imbalance:
1) Continue isolating to the specific component (connector, broken conductor strands,
degraded relay contact) by:
a) Thermal Imaging - Infrared (IR) camera easily identifies current imbalance,
voltage imbalance (drop) via heat signature.
b) Clamp-on ammeter - Verify current imbalance identified by IR camera.
c) Multi-meter - Verify voltage imbalance identified by IR camera. For example,
test voltage drop across relay contacts, and connections.

20-10-79-270-801Ultrasonic Leak Detection ChecksPDF p. 557

2. Ultrasonic Leak Detection Checks
(Figure 201, Figure 202)
A. General
(1) Recommended Equipment
(a) An ultrasonic leak probe, SPL-1473, is the recommend equipment. When performing
ultrasonic leak detection, use a leak detector that meets or exceeds ASTM E1002.
(b) An acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, is the recommend equipment. Recommend
using a camera with an adjustable frequency range between 2kHz to 50kHz.
(2) Usage
(a) An ultrasonic leak probe, SPL-1473, converts and amplifies inaudible ultrasonic sounds
into audible “natural” sounds by lowering the received frequency into the audible range.
The unaided human ear can only detect sound between 20 Hz and 20 kHz; well below
what is required to detect pressure leaks that are normally found in the ultrasonic 35kHz
to 45kHz range.
1) Detect pressure leaks, vacuum leaks and hydraulic bypassing.
a) Provides effective indication and location of leaks. When a gas or liquid
escapes through a crack from a high-pressure system to a low-pressure
system it results in turbulence, which produces ultrasound.
(b) An acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, provides a means to quickly sweep a wide area
to detect and locate leaks in compressed air, compressed gas, and vacuum systems. The
frequency range covers 2kHz to 52kHz with a maximum operating distance of 164 ft
(50 m). The acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, has a visible light camera that captures
a live-view image of the inspection area, while the acoustic sensor-array aligns a
sound-source heatmap with the image.
(3) Images in this task are examples only. The images may not agree with your airplane model or
airplane configuration.

(1) Do the cabin pressurization leak test as follows:
NOTE: Two persons are necessary for this task. One person examines the airplane with the
acoustic camera from out of the airplane, while the other person in the airplane uses
the ultrasonic detector to identify the leakage.
(a) Do the cabin pressurization (TASK 21-00-00-800-801).
(b) Examine the windows, doors, and other possible leak locations with the acoustic digital
camera, COM-18702, to find the leakage.
1) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(c) Speak with the person in the airplane to identify the location of the leaks with the
ultrasonic leak probe, SPL-1473.
NOTE: Use an ultrasonic leak detector with the recommended sensitivity.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-002
(2) Do the air conditioning leak check as follows:
20-10-79
(a) Operate the air conditioning (TASK 21-00-00-800-801).
(b) Examine the packs and ducting with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, for
possible leaks.
1) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(c) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak probe,
SPL-1473.
NOTE: Some valves have pressure bleed orifices that can possibly show as leaks. If you
are not sure, identify the leaking orifice and compare with the other side.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-003
(3) Do the bleed air leak check as follows:
(a) For the airframe do the following steps:
1) Operate the bleed air (TASK 36-00-00-860-801).
2) Examine the aircraft with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, for possible
leaks.
a) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you
found are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move
while the user moves.
3) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak
probe, SPL-1473.
NOTE: Once panel is removed, bleed air leaks are easily pinpointed to clamps,
valve body and seals.
(b) For the engine do the following steps:
1) Operate the bleed air (TASK 36-00-00-860-801).
2) Open the Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Controller (PRSOVC) to back
pressure lines and ducts up to the High Pressure Shutoff Valve (HPSV)
(TASK 36-00-00-860-805).
3) Examine the engine with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, for possible
leaks.
a) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you
found are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move
while the user moves.
4) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak
probe, SPL-1473.
NOTE: Some valves have pressure bleed orifices that possibly show as leaks. If
you are not sure, identify the leaking orifice and compare with the other
side.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-004
(4) Do the hydraulic system bypassing check as follows:
(a) Operate the hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-801).
20-10-79
1) Examine the hydraulic valves/lines with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, for
possible bypassing.
2) If you find the bypassing, you must identify the location of the bypassing with the
ultrasonic leak probe, SPL-1473.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-005
(5) Do the parking brake bleed down issue as follows:
(a) Operate the hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-801).
NOTE: It can be necessary to occasionally re-pressurize the system to do all of the leak
check.
(b) Set the parking brake.
(c) Examine the pressure return lines with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702, for
possible leaks.
1) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(d) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak probe,
SPL-1473.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-006
(6) Do the pitot static check as follows:
(a) Increase pitot and static to the maximum test pressures (TASK 34-11-00-790-802).
(b) Examine the pitot and static lines and components with the acoustic digital camera,
COM-18702, for possible leaks.
1) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(c) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak probe,
SPL-1473.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-007
(7) Do the oxygen system leak check as follows:
(a) Examine the oxygen lines and components with the acoustic digital camera, COM-18702,
for possible leaks.
1) Make sure that you do not contact with the oxygen lines or components.
2) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(b) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak probe,
SPL-1473.
SUBTASK 20-10-79-790-008
(8) Do the leak check of evacuation slides, tires and other pressurized components as follows:
(a) Examine the slides, tires or other pressurized components with the acoustic digital
camera, COM-18702, for possible leaks.
20-10-79
1) When you find the leaks, move the camera to make sure that the leaks you found
are not reflections.
NOTE: Leaks will stay stable while the user moves. Reflections will move while the
user moves.
(b) If you find leaks, you must identify the location of the leaks with the ultrasonic leak probe,
SPL-1473.

2. Intermittent Wiring Special Detailed Inspection
(Figure 201, Figure 202, Figure 203)
A. General
(1) This task shows how to locate the source of an intermittent wiring fault using the wire shake
inspection.
(2) This test will require a minimum of two people. One person monitors the multimeters and
another to shake the wire.
(3) A value change in resistance on one of the multimeters will find the intermittent fault condition.
(4) Most of the intermittent wiring faults will be found at the connectors, terminals, and splices.
(5) Most of the intermittent wiring faults will be found outside of the fuselage pressure seal.
(6) These are the necessary tools to do this task:
(a) Multimeter(s) - digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793
(b) Meter Lead Kit - meter lead kit, SPL-15027
B. References
Reference Title
20-40-12-000-804 Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Removal (P/B 201)
20-40-12-400-804 Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Installation
(P/B 201)
24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201)
24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.

D. Prepare for the Wire Shake Inspection.
NOTE: Preparation is very important to decrease the airplane ground time and should be done
before the airplane is grounded.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-300-001
(1) Use the following applicable documents to find the locations of the wire bundles and Line
Replaceable Unit (LRU) which cause the intermittent faults:
(a) Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM)
(b) Fault Isolation Manual (FIM)
(c) Wiring Diagram Manual (WDM)
(d) Fleet T eam Digest (FTD)
(e) Standard Wiring Practices Manual (SWPM)
(f) Service Letter (SL)
(g) Maintenance Tip (MT)
(h) Other service document.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-300-002
(2) Prepare the applicable pages from the documents.
NOTE: The pages will provide quick reference on the airplane during troubleshooting.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-860-001
(3) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
NOTE: Electrical power must be off to prevent incorrect fault indications or fault messages
from occurring.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-300-003
(4) Get access to the applicable wire bundles and LRUs.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-300-004
(5) Select the applicable troubleshooting configuration:
20-10-80
(a) Circuits Containing One Wire
(b) Circuits Containing Two Wires
(c) ARINC 429 Data Bus Wires.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-300-005
(6) Continue to the steps for the applicable troubleshooting configuration.
E. Circuits Containing One Wire
(Figure 201)
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS, OR OTHER CONDUCTORS. IF
YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-001
(1) Disconnect the applicable electrical connector D1 from the applicable LRU 1.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-002
(2) Do this task on the applicable LRU 1: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Installation,
TASK 20-40-12-400-804.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-003
(3) Examine the electrical connector D1 for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-004
(4) Do these steps to connect the multimeter M1 (digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793) to the
connector D1:
(a) Put the multimeter M1 to the resistance function.
(b) Connect the lead A from the multimeter M1 to the correct pin/socket A of the electrical
connector D1.
(c) Connect the lead B from the multimeter M1 to the airplane ground or to the correct pin/
socket B of the electrical connector D1 which is grounded.
NOTE: The multimeter M1 will read the resistance of the LRU 2 to the airplane ground.
The LRU 2 can be a sensor, valve, actuator, transducer, proximity switch, or
some other component.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-005
(5) If the LRU 2 does not have a value of resistance, do the following steps:
(a) Remove the LRU 2 from the electrical connector D5.
(b) Examine the electrical connector D5 for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
(c) Install the Load Resistor (47 ohm) to the correct pins/sockets on the electrical connector
D5.
NOTE: The multimeter M1 will read the resistance (47ohm) of the Load Resistor.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-006
(6) If necessary, the Jumper Adapter can be used for the continuity check with the multimeter's
resistance function or continuity function.
NOTE: With the multimeter's resistance function, movement of connectors, terminal blocks,
wire bundles will momentarily increase resistance.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-007
(7) Continue to the Procedure for the Wire Shake Inspection.
20-10-80
F . Circuits Containing Two Wires
(Figure 202)
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS, OR OTHER CONDUCTORS. IF
YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-008
(1) Disconnect the applicable electrical connector D1 from the applicable LRU 1.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-009
(2) Examine the electrical connector D1 for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-010
(3) Do this task on the applicable LRU 1: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Installation,
TASK 20-40-12-400-804.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-011
(4) Do these steps to connect two multimeters M1 and M2 (two digital/analog multimeters,
COM-1793) to the electrical connector D1:
(a) Put the multimeters M1 and M2 to the resistance function.
(b) Connect the lead A from the multimeter M1 to the correct pin/socket A of the electrical
connector D1.
NOTE: The multimeter M1 will read the resistance of the LRU 2 . The LRU 2 can be a
sensor, valve, actuator, transducer, proximity switch, or some other component.
(c) Connect the lead B from the Y Junction to the correct pin/socket B of the electrical
connector D1.
(d) Connect the lead C from the multimeter M2 to the airplane ground.
NOTE: The multimeter M2 should read an open circuit and will check for a short circuit to
the airplane ground.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-012
(5) If the LRU 2 does not have a value of resistance, do the following steps:
NOTE: The multimeter M1 will read the resistance (47 ohm) of the Load Resistor.
NOTE: The multimeter M2 should read an open circuit and will examine for a short circuit to
the airplane ground.
(a) Remove the LRU 2 from the electrical connector D5.
(b) Do this task on the applicable LRU 2: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover
Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-804.
(c) Examine the electrical connector D5 for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
(d) Install the Load Resistor (47 ohm) to the correct pins/sockets on the electrical connector
D5.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-013
(6) Continue to the Procedure for the Wire Shake Inspection.
G. ARINC 429 Data Bus Wires
(Figure 203)
20-10-80
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS, OR OTHER CONDUCTORS. IF
YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-014
(1) Disconnect all the data bus connectors from the applicable LRUs.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-015
(2) Examine the data bus connectors for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-016
(3) Do this task on the applicable LRUs: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Installation,
TASK 20-40-12-400-804.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-017
(4) Do these steps to connect two multimeters M1 and M2 (two digital/analog multimeters,
COM-1793), to the data bus connector D1:
NOTE: The multimeters will be connected to the data bus connector of the LRU 1 that does
not receive the data.
(a) Put the multimeters M1 and M2 to the resistance function.
(b) Connect the lead A from the multimeter M1 to the correct pin/socket A of the data bus
connector D1.
(c) Connect the lead B from the Y Junction to the correct pin/socket B of the data bus
connector D1.
(d) Connect the lead C from the multimeter M2 to the airplane ground.
NOTE: The multimeters M1 and M2 should read open.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-018
(5) If the multimeters M1 and M2 show a high resistance, do the following steps:
NOTE: An LRU is possibly connected to the data bus when the multimeters M1 and M2 show
a high resistance.
(a) Find the applicable LRU(s) that is possibly connected to the data bus.
(b) Remove the applicable LRU(s).
(c) Do this task on the applicable LRU(s): Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover
Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-804.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-019
(6) Examine the data bus connector D10 for bent or broken pins/sockets, dirt, and damage.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-020
(7) Connect the Load Resistor (47 ohm) to the correct pins/sockets on the data bus connector D10
of the LRU 4 that sends the data to the LRU 1 that receives the data.
NOTE: The multimeter M1 will read the resistance (47ohm) of the Load Resistor.
NOTE: The multimeter M2 will examine for a short circuit to the airplane ground.
SUBTASK 20-10-80-760-021
(8) Continue to the Procedure for the Wire Shake Inspection.
20-10-80
H. Procedure for the Wire Shake Inspection
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT TOOLS, TOOL TRAYS, AND OTHER WORK ITEMS ON THE
WIRES. OBJECTS THAT YOU PUT ON THE WIRE BUNDLES, OR THEIR
RELATED COMPONENTS, CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WIRES,
INSULATION AND CONNECTORS.
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT PRESSURE ON THE WIRE BUNDLES, ELECTRONIC
SYSTEMS, OR STRUCTURES IN THE COMPARTMENT . PRESSURE CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO WIRE BUNDLES AND ELECTRICAL CONNECTIONS.
CAUTION
DO NOT CUT , NICK, OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CABLES, THE WIRES,
THE METAL-BRAID SHIELD, OR THE OVER-BRAID. DAMAGE TO THESE
COMPONENTS CAN CAUSE MALFUNCTIONS, OR DAMAGE TO OTHER
EQUIPMENT .
SUBTASK 20-10-80-211-001
(1) To locate the intermittent fault on the wire, do the following steps:
(a) Shake the wire bundle at every connector, terminal, and splice outside the fuselage
pressure seal.
1) If one of the multimeters shows a change in value, replace the defective component
per SWPM.
2) If none of the multimeters show a change in value, continue to the next step.
(b) Shake the wire bundle at every connector, terminal, and splice inside the fuselage
pressure seal.
1) If one of the multimeters shows a change in value, replace the defective component
per SWPM.
2) If none of the multimeters show a change in value, continue to the next step.
(c) Shake the entire wire bundle outside the fuselage pressure seal.
1) If one of the multimeters shows a change in value, replace the defective component
per SWPM.
2) If none of the multimeters show a change in value, continue to the next step.
(d) Shake the entire wire bundle inside the fuselage pressure seal.
1) If one of the multimeters shows a change in value, replace the defective component
per SWPM.
2) If necessary, repeat all of the above steps if none of the multimeters show a change
in value.
(e) When the test is complete, do the following steps:
1) Do this task on the applicable LRU: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover
Removal, TASK 20-40-12-000-804.
2) Reconnect the applicable electrical connector(s) to the applicable LRU(s).
I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 20-10-80-860-002
(1) If necessary, do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.

20-10-91-400-801Control Cables InstallationPDF p. 585

3. Control Cables Installation
(Figure 401), (Figure 402) and (Figure 403)
A. General
(1) If this procedure does not agree with a specified maintenance procedure, use the specified
maintenance procedure.
(2) Detailed data is in Chapter 27 for flight control cables and Chapter 32 for Landing Gear Control
Cables.
(3) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned three to four months into service. This will bring the
tension of the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the
high zinc cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the
Grade B cables.
(4) It is recommended that cable assemblies on each side of a cable loop be replaced at the same
time using the same grade material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.

SUBTASK 20-10-91-420-003
(1) Install the cable.

cable.

routing the new cable.
(c) Pull the old cable out, which pulls the new cable through at the same time.

F . Non-prefabricated Cable Installation
SUBTASK 20-10-91-820-001
(1) Identify the cable you remove.
(a) Refer to the applicable system chapter to prepare a new cable.
(b) Refer to Figure 401, to calculate cable length.
NOTE: The total length of the cable after assembly and the test will be longer than the lengths
of the terminals and the cable before they are assembled. The terminals will be longer
after they are swaged, and the cable will be longer after the proof test. Make sure that
you include an allowance for each of these changes before you cut the cable to the
required length.
SUBTASK 20-10-91-420-004
(2) Install only those fittings that will permit cable installation.
(a) If the wire rope has a nylon jacket, remove the nylon from the end of the wire rope before
you put the rope in the terminal.
1) Remove a length of nylon to give 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) maximum clearance between
the terminal and the jacket after the rope is installed in the terminal.
(b) Put the cut end of the wire rope into the full depth of the bore of the terminal.
1) If the bore of the terminal does not go completely through, make sure that the wire
rope is at the full depth as follows:
a) Measure the depth of the bore.
b) Mark this as a length from the end of the wire rope before you install and
swage the fittings.
(c) T erminals can be staked on the wire rope to keep them in the correct position before they
are swaged.
1) The maximum allowable stake depth after swaging is 0.003 in. (0.076 mm).
20-10-91

Table 402.
